zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Great Falls & Downtown Center, Singac & Route 46 Corridor
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 3.496%, with an equalization ratio of 62.24%.
Public education represents 53.6% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 29.8%.
Average residential assessment is $336,096, producing an average annual tax bill of $11,749.92.

neighborhoods.name: Great Falls & Downtown Center
neighborhoods.character: Historic town center near Passaic River with brick colonials, walkable restaurants, and Montclair State University border
neighborhoods.description: Walkable village core featuring Morris Canal historic park, local dining, and Little Falls train station commuting to NYC.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Balanced mix of retail shops and single-family homes with Passaic Valley regional high school sharing.

neighborhoods.name: Singac & Route 46 Corridor
neighborhoods.character: Residential and commercial neighborhood along Passaic River with historic single-family homes and river parklands
neighborhoods.description: Residential area near Passaic Valley High School campus, experiencing active township flood mitigation and buyouts.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Subject to flood insurance adjustments and river basin capital infrastructure bonds.

equityAnalysis.summary: Little Falls Township maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Little Falls Township, homeowners pay an average of $11,749.92 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 9.92% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 62.24%, assessed values average ~62.24% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 53.6% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 29.8%, and Passaic County claims 16.6%.
